data.title: Product of Array Except Self
data.summary:
Input: An array of integers nums.
Output: An array of integers where each element at index i is the product of all elements in nums except nums[i].
Rules: Must run in O(n) time complexity and without using the division operation.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer

data.generator_code:
def generate(rng, n):
    # Values must be mostly 1 or -1 to respect the 32-bit prefix/suffix product constraint
    nums = [rng.choice([-1, 1]) for _ in range(n)]
    if n > 5:
        # Introduce a few small non-identity values or a zero
        idx1 = rng.randint(0, n - 1)
        nums[idx1] = rng.choice([-3, -2, 0, 2, 3])
        idx2 = rng.randint(0, n - 1)
        if idx2 != idx1:
            nums[idx2] = rng.choice([-2, 2])
    return [nums]

def generate_worst(rng, n):
    # Alternating 1 and -1 forces the full calculation across the entire array
    nums = [1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1 for i in range(n)]
    return [nums]

events.label: Solver: design the algorithm
events.detail: Prefix and Suffix Products in $O(1)$ Extra Space · claims O(n) time

data.approach: Prefix and Suffix Products in $O(1)$ Extra Space
data.key_insight: The product of all elements except the one at index $i$ is the product of all elements to the left of $i$ (prefix product) multiplied by the product of all elements to the right of $i$ (suffix product). We can compute these dynamically in two passes without using division.

steps.title: Initialize the Output Array
steps.detail: Create an output array `ans` of the same length as `nums`, initialized with 1s. This array will temporarily store the prefix products and eventually the final result.

steps.title: Compute Prefix Products
steps.detail: Iterate through the array from left to right. For each index `i` (from 1 to $n-1$), set `ans[i] = ans[i-1] * nums[i-1]`. This stores the product of all elements before index `i` in `ans[i]`.

steps.title: Compute Suffix Products and Finalize
steps.detail: Iterate through the array from right to left (from $n-1$ down to 0) while maintaining a running suffix product variable `suffix_product` initialized to 1. At each step, multiply `ans[i]` by `suffix_product`, then update `suffix_product` by multiplying it with `nums[i]`.

data.overview: This algorithm calculates the product of all elements in an array except self without division by making two passes over the array. The first pass computes left prefix products, and the second pass multiplies them by right suffix products on the fly.
data.intuition: Imagine standing at a person in a line. To know the product of everyone's heights except yours, you multiply the product of everyone to your left by the product of everyone to your right.

flow_nodes.label: Initialize ans array
flow_nodes.detail: Set up the result array filled with ones and get array length n.

flow_nodes.label: Prefix loop
flow_nodes.detail: Iterate forward from index 1 to n-1 to compute prefix products.

flow_nodes.label: Initialize suffix_product
flow_nodes.detail: Set suffix_product to 1 before starting the backward pass.

flow_nodes.label: Suffix loop
flow_nodes.detail: Iterate backward from n-1 down to 0, updating ans and suffix_product.

flow_nodes.label: Return ans
flow_nodes.detail: Return the final computed product array.

pitfalls: Using division, which violates the problem constraints.
Forgetting to initialize the suffix_product variable to 1.
Off-by-one errors in the loop ranges for prefix or suffix passes.

events.label: Coach: pattern, brute force and its bottleneck
events.detail: Pattern: Prefix and Suffix Products · 3 hints

data.pattern_summary: Precomputing cumulative products from the left and right directions allows you to find the product of all elements outside of any index in O(1) time.

pattern_options.name: Prefix and Suffix Products
pattern_options.feedback: Correct. Separating the elements into left-side products and right-side products avoids nested loops and division.

pattern_options.name: Hash map lookup
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. A hash map helps track frequencies or indices, but does not help calculate products across array ranges.

pattern_options.name: Two pointers
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. Two pointers usually work for ordered arrays or searching from extremes inward, not for computing continuous products.

pattern_options.name: Sliding window
pattern_options.feedback: Incorrect. A sliding window requires a contiguous subarray, whereas this problem excludes a single element while including everything else.

signals.phrase: product of all elements in nums except nums[i]
signals.hint: This means for every index, you need to combine elements from both its left side and right side.
You cannot simply take the total product of the array and divide by nums[i], forcing you to build the products from components.

data.brute_force_idea: For every element in the array, run a second loop over the entire array to multiply every other element together, storing the result in a new array.
data.brute_force_why: There are two nested loops of size n, leading to n times n operations.
data.bottleneck: The inner loop re-multiplies almost the exact same set of numbers for every single index i, repeating a massive amount of multiplication work.
bottleneck_hints: Look at what elements you are multiplying together for index i versus index i+1.
Notice how much overlap there is in the numbers multiplied for adjacent indices.
Ask yourself if you can save previous multiplication results instead of starting from scratch at every index.

events.label: Coach: why the complexity is what it is

data.insight: The brute force approach repeatedly recalculates products for every element using nested loops, leading to O(n^2) time. The optimized solution removes this bottleneck by building prefix products in a single forward pass and accumulating suffix products in a single backward pass, using the output array itself for storage.

derivation.note: Allocates the result array of size n once.
Loops from 1 to n-1 to populate prefix products.
Performs constant-time multiplication on each iteration.
Loops backward from n-1 down to 0.
Multiplies the existing prefix product by the running suffix product.

data.time_summary: Adding the costs gives 1 + 1 + n + (n-1) + 1 + (n+1) + n + n + 1 = 5n + 5 steps. As n grows, the dominant term is n, making the time complexity O(n), which matches the measured evidence.
data.space_summary: The output array ans is required by the problem statement and takes O(n) space. The variable suffix_product takes O(1) space, meaning extra memory beyond the output array is O(1).
data.takeaway: When you need to compute values dependent on all other elements excluding the current one, compute cumulative products from both the left and right directions in separate passes.
mistakes: Using division to solve the problem, which violates the problem constraints.
Forgetting that the output array counts toward space complexity if not handled carefully, though returning it is required.
Off-by-one errors when setting up the loop ranges for prefix and suffix passes.
